packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
Packet 17 - blind image reading (unverified)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading for this packet. Beyond the rules: I cropped and enlarged the native tiles with PIL (2x) for reading. I opened no other files.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- A small rectangular parchment fragment, about 9 x 3.5-4 cm by the ruler. It is cut on all four sides, so only part of one column survives. No margins, running titles or column boundaries are visible, apart from a narrow strip at the left of face A that may be the inner margin or gutter edge (it shows a brownish stain).
- 8 lines per face, in a small gothic textualis book hand in brown-black ink. The writing on both faces is rubbed and faded.
- Red: on each face there are small red initials (or red-stroked letters) with a red pen flourish extending from them, set inline at the start of new sections in mid-line. Some letters are touched in red and there is red ruling. Face A has red initials at line 3 ("M"?) and line 8; face B has one at line 2 ("N").
- Face A has many short abbreviated reference tags of the shape "ex(tra?) . de [title]" and "c . [incipit]" between passages. Tentative interpretation: a text with cross-references to titled sections ("de iudeis", "de raptoribus"...), or a summary or compilation in which each item ends with a reference. Face B reads as continuous prose with "regni nostri Anglie(?)", "comes ul baro", "redimi", "plegi-", which points to a legal/regulatory text. This is interpretation only.
- No interlinear or marginal glosses visible.
- Cracks/holes run across line 4-5 on both faces.

SELECTED SPANS
I read all 8 lines on both faces (the full fragment). I could not read: the left third of face A lines 5-8, which is badly rubbed, and parts of face B lines 1-4 at the left.

TRANSCRIPTION (line numbers from the top of the respective native tile; each line is cut at both ends)

Face A (image-002; overview image-001)
image-002 l.1: ...iar(?) . ex . de iudeis . c(?) ſure(?) iudei(?) . Cum etiam(?) in ma(?)na(?)s(?) e(?) . g(?)...     [a faint line of letter-tops is cut off above this one]
image-002 l.2: ...cōītes(?) . r . f . de detinamentis(?) . ex . de raptorib(us) . c . v(?) . ex . de...     ["detinamentis" is uncertain and could be "detrimentis"; "c . v" could be "c . u" / "e . v"]
image-002 l.3: ...postulasti . [red initial with flourish] Medicus nolens iudic(are)(?) ꝛ(et?) iudicet(?) [..]ar(?)mi(?) ni[..]...     [after "Medicus" the word reads "nolens"; the next could be "indicare" or "iudicare"; "iudicet" could be "indicet"; the 2-3 words before "mī" are rubbed]
image-002 l.4: ...[..]uni(?)[.] q(ui)no(?)rt(?) mediū(?) [..]ēq(?) que(?) ꝛ confessione(?) [..]im(?) . ex . de...     ["confessione" is fairly clear; the rest is uncertain]
image-002 l.5: ...[..] ...firmitas(?) . [C?]lerici(?)/[S?]imo(n)iac(us)(?) ... ve(?) t(?)ribus(?) ꝑ(?) vi(?)...     [the left half is rubbed; there is a hole above "firmitas"; "simoniacus" is uncertain, and so is "de testibus/tribus"]
image-002 l.6: ...[.] [illegible] ... [..]bus(?) in sacris ordin(ibus)(?)...     ["in sacris ord-" is fairly clear; the left 2/3 of the line is rubbed]
image-002 l.7: ...[illegible] ... [..] ad(?) [..]atio(?) aut posita semel(?)...     ["aut posita semel" is fairly clear; "semel" could be "simul"]
image-002 l.8: ...ex . de cl(?)[..] in uio(?)r(?) . c . [..]e(?) re(?) . [red initial with flourish] I(?)[n/u]ue(?)ns(?) . et(?) clericus(?)...     [faint; "ex . de" is clear at the start; the word after the red initial is uncertain]

Face B (image-004; overview image-003)
image-004 l.1: ...e[x?] . [..] [..]a[..]tur(?)[..] [..] hōis (hominis) q(?)ua nocte(?) ꝯ(?)nominu(?)[..]...     ["hōis" is clear; "qua nocte" is uncertain and could be "quam vere", "quanto(?)"]
image-004 l.2: ...[..]i(?) min(?)[.]i(?) uos(?) [..]e(?) . [..]a(?)r(?) ... [..]ā(?) de suo po(?)ct(?) . [red initial with flourish] Nul[..]...     ["de suo" is clear; "poct" could be "potest/pot(er)it"; "Nul-" is the start of a new section after the red initial]
image-004 l.3: ...[..]ba(?)uo(?) iudici(?)[..] [..]ēm(?)d(?)ꝫ(?) ꝑ nemo(?) / ꝑ uenus(?)[..]e(?)ō(?) om(n)is(?) [..]ē(?)...     [very uncertain; superscript marks over several words]
image-004 l.4: ...[..]a(?) Cor(?)ama(?) fieri(?) ꝛ . Similis(?)/Summ(?) de cr(?)i(m)i(n)e(?) ꝗ(?)[..] ꝯ(?)na(?)d(?)nat(us)(?) . [..]...     ["de cr(i)mine" is uncertain; "condempnatus" is a guess from the letter shapes, not confirmed]
image-004 l.5: ...[..]mu(?)tagio(?) . sicut(?) vn(?) redimi(?)[.] [..]o(?)ry(?) [..] [illegible] ... [..]h(?)ā(?) redimi(?)...     [a hole and rubbing in the centre; "redim-" appears twice]
image-004 l.6: ...[..]i(?)marcat(?)/[..]imaretur(?) . in p(er)sona(?) n(ost)ra(?) ꝑ(?) uimictu(?)/vinculu(?) ꝛ v(?)na(?) dece(m)(?) . r . si post...     ["in p(er)sona n(ost)ra" is moderately clear; "si post" is clear]
image-004 l.7: ...r(?) die(m)(?) plegiōs(?)/pleg(ios)(?) [..]ione(?) postmo(dum)(?)cecat(?) de p(er)sona n(ost)ra suā(?) [..]e(?) ab...     ["pleg-" with a superscript "e"/abbreviation; "de p(er)sona n(ost)ra" is fairly clear; "postmo cecat" is uncertain]
image-004 l.8: ...r(?) regni n(ost)ri Anglie(?) . [enlarged initial, not red] Q(?)uī(?)/Cu(m)(?) [..] cecid(er)it(?)/ceperit(?) ꝯ(?)itie(?) comes ul(?) baro...     ["regni" and "n(ost)ri" are clear; "Angl-" with an abbreviation is fairly clear; "comes" and "baro" are clear; "ul" may be "uel" or "ut"]

LIMITATIONS
- The fragment is cut on all sides, so every line is incomplete at both ends. The line order between faces is not established.
- The surface is heavily rubbed, especially the left half of face A lines 5-8 and face B lines 1-4.
- Many of my word readings carry a "(?)" and should not be used for matching without checking.
- The best spans for a source match: face A "ex . de iudeis", "ex . de raptorib(us)", "postulasti . Medicus nolens ...", "in sacris ordin-", "aut posita semel"; face B "de suo po[test?] . Nul-", "in p(er)sona n(ost)ra ... si post", "de p(er)sona n(ost)ra", "regni n(ost)ri Anglie ... comes ul baro".
- Suggested next step: UV or raking light for the rubbed areas.
